body.statement: The replacement result gives \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and therefore \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Hence \(P(\mathcal E_n)\to1\) under \(\inf_{c\in\mathcal C}\lambda_{\min}(H_c)\ge h\). On \(\mathcal E_n\), \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_c)\ge h/2\) for every \(c\), so \(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}=\widehat H_c\) and \((\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}=\widehat H_c^{-1}\) uniformly over \(\mathcal C\). Thus the measurable ridge fallback makes every finite-sample plug-in influence, covariance, and multiplier object total without changing any limiting law.
body.justification: A declared totalization convention is necessary because a finite-sample empirical Hessian can be singular even when the population path is uniformly curved.
body.gap: FangRidderXie2026 states fixed-penalty asymptotics and does not need a pathwise totalization convention for the proposed shared-multiplier implementation.
body.consumer: Every reported covariance, multiplier draw, and regret draw remains mathematically defined on every sample, while the maintained curvature shows that the fallback is asymptotically inactive.
